# Design Document

## Overview

Gradients become a paint type. `Style.fill` / `Style.stroke` change from `str | None` to `Paint = str | LinearGradient | RadialGradient | None`. Gradients are frozen values that keep their SVG units; the renderer resolves them against the shape's local bounding box into cached Skia shaders; the reader resolves references (`url(#id)`, `href` chains, error rules) into those values; the SVG writer emits them once into `<defs>`; `.p2s` stores them as objects in the existing `fill` / `stroke` fields. Patterns, gradient creation and on-canvas editing are out of scope (requirements).

```
models/shapes.py        GradientStop, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, Paint, flat_color(); sanitized() handles gradients
formats/svg_gradients.py   pure reader side: reference + href chain + defaults + error rules -> Paint
formats/svg_reader.py   _paint/_color use it; bakes the element matrix into the gradient (see Matrix rule)
formats/svg_paint.py    writer side: PaintDefs collector (dedupe, ids, <defs>, url(#id))
formats/svg.py          threads the collector through _shape_element / _style_attributes
formats/p2s.py          encode_paint / decode_paint; version 8
render/gradients.py     gradient + local bounds -> skia shader
render/paths.py         PathCache.shaders(shape): cached (fill, stroke) shaders per shape
render/scene.py         _paints(...) sets the shader instead of a colour
views/style_editor.py   _PaintRow shows a gradient swatch; flat pick replaces
```

## Steering Document Alignment

No steering docs; `CLAUDE.md` rules apply: no Qt below `views/`, import direction `models <- geometry <- render <- editing <- tools <- views` with `formats` on models + geometry only, shapes frozen and changed through `dataclasses.replace`, explicit p2s encoders (version bump + migration + sample + `docs/file-format.md` row), paint defaults equal to SVG, no new per-frame cost, `Note` strings through `ngettext`/`de.po`, comments only for a non-obvious why.

## Code Reuse Analysis

### Existing Components to Leverage
- **`svg_reader._Reader.ids`**: the document-wide id map `<use>` already uses; gradients resolve through it.
- **`_Reader.style(inherited, element)`**: cascade incl. CSS (Level 1) for stop colours and `color` for `currentColor`.
- **`svg_lengths` + `_Reader._length`**: lengths and `%` against the current `Viewport` (Level 2 stack).
- **`svg_values.parse_transform`**, `geometry.affine` (`compose`, `invert`, `apply`): `gradientTransform` and baking.
- **`PathCache`**: entries valid while the stored frozen shape equals the current one; shaders join that scheme.
- **`models.shapes.sanitized`**: range-fixing for p2s decoding and reader output stays in one place.
- **`resvg` generator check** (`tests/formats/test_svg_generator.py`): extended to gradients.

### Integration Points
- `Style.fill` / `.stroke` consumers (audited): `render/scene.py` (`_filled`, `_stroked`, `_paints`), `render/paths.py` (`_bounds`), `render/hit_test.py`, `formats/svg.py`, `formats/p2s.py`, `views/style_editor.py`, `editing/operations/style.py` (typing only), `formats/svg_reader.py`. Truthiness checks (`bool(style.fill)`, `if style.stroke`) keep working because a gradient dataclass is truthy. The two places that treat the value as a string are `parse_color(style.fill)` in `scene._paints` and `style.fill or "none"` in `svg._style_attributes`; both go through the new helpers.
- Booleans, Composites, `restyle_shape`, paste style copy `Style`/fields whole, so gradients pass through unchanged.

## Architecture

### Modular Design Principles
- **One module per job**: resolving a reference (reader), writing (writer), building a shader (render), model values. None imports from a layer above.
- **Values, not references**: the model holds no ids and no registry; equal gradients compare equal, the writer dedupes, the reader hands the same frozen object to every shape that uses one reference.

```mermaid
graph LR
    SVG[SVG file] --> R[svg_reader + svg_gradients]
    R --> M[Style.fill / stroke: Paint]
    P2S[.p2s] --> M
    M --> Sh[render/gradients -> skia shader, cached in PathCache]
    M --> W[svg_paint PaintDefs -> defs + url]
    M --> E[p2s encode_paint]
    M --> UI[style_editor swatch]
```

## Components and Interfaces

### Component 1: Model (`models/shapes.py`)
- **Purpose:** the paint values; range fixing.
- **Interfaces:**
  - `GradientStop(offset: float, color: str, opacity: float = 1.0)`; `color` is `#rrggbb`.
  - `LinearGradient(x1, y1, x2, y2, stops, units="objectBoundingBox", spread="pad", transform=IDENTITY_TRANSFORM)`, `RadialGradient(cx, cy, r, fx, fy, stops, units, spread, transform)`. `units` is `"objectBoundingBox" | "userSpaceOnUse"`, `spread` is `"pad" | "reflect" | "repeat"`. Coordinates are fractions of the box (objectBoundingBox) or user-space numbers.
  - `Gradient = LinearGradient | RadialGradient`, `Paint = str | Gradient | None`.
  - `flat_color(paint) -> str | None`: a colour string as is, the first stop's colour for a gradient, `None` for none. Used by UI and any code that needs one colour.
  - `sanitized`: sorts out gradients — stops clamped to 0..1 and made non-decreasing, opacity clamped, at most `MAX_STOPS` (1024) kept, empty stops → paint `None`, unknown enum → defaults, non-finite numbers → SVG defaults, `r < 0` → `None`, focal point outside the circle moved onto it, non-invertible `transform` → identity.
- **Dependencies:** none new.

### Component 2: Reader resolver (`formats/svg_gradients.py`)
- **Purpose:** from a `url(#id)` reference to a `Paint`, applying the SVG rules; pure (no document walking beyond what is passed in), testable without the reader.
- **Interfaces:** `resolve_gradient(element, ids, stop_style, length) -> Paint`, plus `class Reference` helpers for the `href` chain.
  - `stop_style(element) -> dict[str, str]` and `length(text, axis_or_fraction, ...)` are callables the reader passes in (cascade and lengths), so the module doesn't import the reader.
  - Chain: starting from the referenced element walk `href` up to 16 steps (set of visited elements, cycle ends the chain). Each attribute takes the first element in the chain that has it and **is of the right type** (`x1…y2` from linear ones, `cx cy r fx fy` from radial ones, `gradientUnits gradientTransform spreadMethod` from either). Stops come from the first element in the chain that has `<stop>` children.
  - Defaults and error rules of Requirement 2.5: no stops → `None`; one stop → flat `str` (stop opacity is multiplied into `fill_opacity` by the reader, which returns it with the colour like `_color` does); degenerate vector or `r == 0` → last stop colour; `r < 0` → invalid → fallback; wrong element type (a `<pattern>` or `<rect>` as target) → fallback.
  - Stops: `offset` number or `%`, clamped, forced non-decreasing; `stop-color`/`stop-opacity` through `stop_style`; `currentColor` resolved by the same cascade; colour parsed by the reader's existing colour function (moved to `svg_values` so both use it).
  - `color-interpolation: linearRGB` on the gradient chain's first element is reported to the reader (return value or callback) for the note.
- **Memoisation:** by `(element id, viewport width, viewport height)` in the reader; fractions and `%`-free user-space gradients reuse the same frozen object for every shape.
- **Dependencies:** `models.shapes`, `formats.svg_values`, `geometry.affine`.

### Component 3: Reader integration (`formats/svg_reader.py`)
- **Purpose:** call Component 2 from `_color`, replace the grey placeholder for linear/radial gradients, and place the gradient in the shape's space.
- **Interfaces:** `_color` returns `(Paint, alpha)`; `_paint` stays the single place that builds a `Style`. Patterns keep returning grey and raise `Note.PATTERN` (renamed from `GRADIENT`, wording "pattern(s) painted grey").
- **Matrix rule.** A gradient is defined in the *user space of the shape element*. The reader bakes some of the element matrix `m` into geometry (rect/ellipse with translate-only `m`, every path, whatever `transform_shape` normalises). After the shape is built, with `T` the final `shape.transform` and `B = T⁻¹ ∘ m` the part that was baked into the geometry:
  - `userSpaceOnUse`: `gradient.transform = B ∘ gradientTransform` (identity `B` — the common case — changes nothing).
  - `objectBoundingBox`: kept as is when `B` is only a translation plus positive scales (the bounding box of the baked geometry is `B` of the original box). Otherwise (rotation, skew, mirroring baked into a path) it is converted to `userSpaceOnUse` using the box of `B⁻¹(baked outline)` computed with `geometry` (tight bounds of the segments), then `B` applied as above.
  - Text keeps `objectBoundingBox` unconverted (its box needs fonts, which live in `render/`); documented approximation: a rotated or skewed baked text keeps the gradient direction in its own box.
  - A `fill` and `stroke` gradient are both adjusted this way. `_shape` calls one helper `_place_paint(shape, m)` after construction; it returns the shape with the adjusted style (`dataclasses.replace`).
- **Notes:** `Note.COLOR_INTERPOLATION` ("colours are interpolated in sRGB") when a used gradient says `linearRGB`; stop cap exceeded or `r < 0` use `Note.INVALID_VALUE`.
- **`display: none`:** gradient lookups ignore `display` on the gradient and its ancestors (rendering of `<defs>` content is skipped by `_NOT_RENDERED`, which already lists the gradient tags).

### Component 4: Renderer (`render/gradients.py`, `render/paths.py`, `render/scene.py`)
- **Purpose:** shader per paint, cached with the shape.
- **Interfaces:**
  - `gradient_shader(paint, bounds: skia.Rect) -> skia.Shader | None`: `bounds` is the shape's **local** geometry bounds (without stroke). Returns `None` for objectBoundingBox with a zero-sized box (nothing drawn).
  - Matrix: `localMatrix = box ∘ gradientTransform` where `box` maps the unit square to `bounds` for objectBoundingBox and is identity for userSpaceOnUse; `to_skia_matrix` converts.
  - Linear → `skia.GradientShader.MakeLinear`. Radial → `MakeTwoPointConical(start=(fx, fy), 0, end=(cx, cy), r)`; `fx, fy == cx, cy` uses `MakeRadial`. Tile modes: `kClamp`, `kMirror`, `kRepeat`. Colours are `Color4f` with stop opacity as alpha, interpolated unpremultiplied (Skia default; SVG's rule), positions the stop offsets.
  - `PathCache.shaders(shape) -> tuple[skia.Shader | None, skia.Shader | None]`: (fill, stroke), stored like `_strokes` (valid while the shape is equal), `prune` clears them. Shapes without a gradient never touch it.
  - Local bounds: `RectShape` / `EllipseShape` from their fields, `TextShape` from the untransformed text outline (`render/text.py`), paths and Composites from the cached world path (their transform is identity). Groups have no paint.
  - `scene._paints(style, opacity, shaders)`: a colour string as today (`parse_color`); a gradient sets `paint.setShader(shader)`; `fill_opacity * opacity` still goes through `setAlphaf` (it multiplies the shader's alpha, Skia semantics); a `None` shader skips that paint. `_filled` / `_stroked` stay plain truthiness.
  - Because shaders live in the shape's local space and rects/ellipses/text are drawn inside `canvas.concat(shape.transform)`, userSpaceOnUse gradients follow the shape's transform as SVG says. Gestures with `Overlay.matrix` or `live` shapes need no change: recorded pictures keep the shader, and `live` shapes get their own cache entry.
- **Dependencies:** `skia`, `models`.

### Component 5: SVG writer (`formats/svg_paint.py`, `formats/svg.py`)
- **Purpose:** gradients to `<defs>` once.
- **Interfaces:** `class PaintDefs`: `attribute(paint) -> str` returns `none`, the colour, or `url(#gradN)` and registers a gradient the first time (dict keyed by the frozen value → id; ids `grad1…` in first-use order, stable for the same document); `element() -> ET.Element | None` builds `<defs>` with `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` and `<stop>` children, attributes only where not default (`gradientUnits` when `userSpaceOnUse`, `spreadMethod` when not `pad`, `gradientTransform` through `transform_attr`'s matrix formatting). Stop opacity is written as `stop-opacity` only when below 1.
  - `write_svg` / `write_shapes_svg` create the collector, pass it down `_shape_element(shape, defs)` → `_style_attributes(style, defs)`, and insert `defs.element()` as the first child of the root after serialising shapes (before layers).
  - Composite parts written into `<metadata>` register their gradients through the same collector.
  - Text with an `objectBoundingBox` gradient is written as is; other viewers' text box differs a little from our outline box (documented approximation; text is left out of the resvg pixel comparison for gradients).
- **Dependencies:** `models`, `formats.svg_page.number_text`.

### Component 6: `.p2s` (`formats/p2s.py`, `formats/p2s_migrations.py`)
- **Purpose:** keep gradients in files.
- **Interfaces:** `encode_paint(paint) -> str | None | dict`, `decode_paint(value, where) -> Paint` replacing `_color` for `fill` / `stroke`. Object form: `{"type": "linear", "x1":…, "y1":…, "x2":…, "y2":…, "stops": [{"offset": 0, "color": "#fff", "opacity": 1}, …], "units": "objectBoundingBox", "spread": "pad", "transform": [a,b,c,d,e,f]}` (units, spread, transform, stop opacity only when not default); radial uses `cx cy r fx fy`. Decoders validate each field with the existing `_field`/`_optional_*` helpers and raise the same file-error type; the result goes through `sanitized`.
- `CURRENT_VERSION` 7 → 8; `MIGRATIONS[7] = _unchanged` (version 8 only adds the optional gradient object in `fill` / `stroke`); docstring line extended; `tests/formats/samples/v8.p2s` generated from a document with each gradient type; row in `docs/file-format.md`.
- Tool styles (`tools.styles`) share `encode_style` / `decode_style`, so they carry gradients too. The clipboard payload uses the same encoders, so copy/paste keeps gradients without further work (verified by a test).

### Component 7: Style editor (`views/style_editor.py`, `views/widgets.py`)
- **Purpose:** don't destroy gradients; show them.
- **Interfaces:** `_PaintRow.set_paint(paint, opacity)` accepts a `Paint`. For a gradient the swatch `ColorButton.set_gradient(stops)` shows a horizontal stop preview (stylesheet `qlineargradient` with the stops; same for radial); the checkbox is on. A colour pick emits the flat hex as today and thereby replaces the gradient. Unrelated field edits go through `set_style(**changes)` that only names its own fields, so the gradient stays. The tooltip says "Gradient: pick a colour to replace it" (`_()`).
- `editing/operations/style.set_fill/set_stroke` accept `Paint` (type annotation only).
- **Dependencies:** `models`.

## Data Models

### Gradient values
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GradientStop:
    offset: float            # 0..1, non-decreasing in the list
    color: str               # "#rrggbb"
    opacity: float = 1.0     # 0..1

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LinearGradient:
    x1: float; y1: float; x2: float; y2: float
    stops: tuple[GradientStop, ...]
    units: GradientUnits = "objectBoundingBox"
    spread: SpreadMethod = "pad"
    transform: Transform = IDENTITY_TRANSFORM

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RadialGradient:
    cx: float; cy: float; r: float; fx: float; fy: float
    stops: tuple[GradientStop, ...]
    units: GradientUnits = "objectBoundingBox"
    spread: SpreadMethod = "pad"
    transform: Transform = IDENTITY_TRANSFORM
```
Defaults of an absent `<linearGradient>` geometry (0, 0, 1, 0 as fractions) and radial (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, fx = cx, fy = cy) live in the reader, not in the dataclass.

## Error Handling

### Error Scenarios
1. **Missing/invalid reference, wrong target type** — fallback colour after `url()`, else `None`; `Note.MISSING_REFERENCE` as for `<use>`. *User sees:* the shape without that paint, a note.
2. **`href` cycle or depth over 16** — chain ends at the last valid element; `Note.CYCLIC_REFERENCE`.
3. **No stops** — paint `None`, no note (SVG: "as if `none`").
4. **One stop / degenerate vector / `r == 0`** — flat colour, no note.
5. **More than `MAX_STOPS` stops, `r < 0`, malformed `gradientTransform`/lengths/offsets** — extra stops dropped / treated as invalid value (default applies), `Note.INVALID_VALUE`; never an exception.
6. **objectBoundingBox on a zero-width or zero-height box** — renderer returns no shader, nothing is drawn; the model keeps the gradient.
7. **Non-finite or non-invertible values in p2s** — `sanitized` resets them; wrong types are file errors like other fields.
8. **Skia refuses a shader** (degenerate matrix) — `gradient_shader` returns `None`; the paint is skipped. Not a try/except over Qt: the arguments are validated before the call.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing
- `tests/models/`: constructing, `sanitized` (offset order, NaN, empty, `MAX_STOPS`, unknown enums, `r < 0`, focal outside circle), equality/hash, `flat_color`.
- `tests/formats/test_svg_gradients.py` (resolver): every default, each attribute inherited through `href` from the right element type, stop-only inheritance, cycle, depth, one stop, no stops, degenerate vector, `%` units, `currentColor`, `stop-color` from CSS, `inherit`, `stop-opacity`, offsets (`%`, out of order, clamp), `color-interpolation` report.
- `tests/formats/test_svg_reader_gradients.py`: the Matrix rule for rect translate-only, rect rotated, path with scale / rotation / mirror (objectBoundingBox kept vs converted), `userSpaceOnUse` under a group transform and nested viewport, shared gradient across shapes (same object), fallback colour, pattern grey with its note.
- `tests/render/test_gradients.py` (CPU surface pixels): linear horizontal/diagonal, radial, focal, `pad`/`reflect`/`repeat`, objectBoundingBox on a non-square rect, userSpaceOnUse after a rotated shape, `gradientTransform`, stroke gradient, stop opacity, `fill_opacity` multiplication, zero-size box draws nothing; `PathCache.shaders` returns the same shader object for an unchanged shape and a new one after a change.
- `tests/formats/test_svg_paint.py` (writer): dedupe of equal gradients, id stability, defaults omitted, `defs` position, valid XML for 1 and 3 stops.
- `tests/formats/test_p2s.py`: round trip each type, bad fields rejected, migration from `v7.p2s`, `v8.p2s` sample opens.
- `tests/editing/test_style.py`: set_style on other fields keeps a gradient; setting a colour replaces it; paste style copies it.
- Architecture test stays green (no Qt/skia below the allowed layers).

### Integration Testing
- Conformance: report on `pservers-grad-*`, `-stops-01-f`, `styling-inherit-*`, curate by eye, add passing ones to `tests/scripts/svg_conformance_pass.txt`; reviewed-but-wrong as `!name # reason`.
- Generator check: gradient documents (linear, radial, focal, spread, units, transformed shape, stroke) saved and rendered by resvg compared with our canvas, as for other paint.
- SVG → `.p2s` → SVG round trip equivalence for every gradient test in the suite.
- Benchmark: `scripts/bench_canvas.py` with 10k gradient-filled shapes vs flat; record both in the task log (first frame pays for shader creation, later frames must match flat fills).

### End-to-End Testing
- `scripts/screenshot_app.py` with a gradient demo shape: read the PNG, check the canvas and the style panel swatch. Headless QTest drive: select a gradient shape, change width/opacity (gradient stays), pick a flat colour (replaced), undo (gradient back).
- `main.py --self-test` unchanged (no new data files or native libraries).
